title: Operator Command Center: unified admin utility and runbook-to-task pipeline
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a centralized Operator Command Center (OCC) that consolidates lightweight admin utilities (CLI + web), converts canonical runbooks into discrete executable tasks, and wires support automation (triage bots, snapshot/rollback hooks). The goal is to reduce MTTR for common incidents, make runbooks auditable and repeatable, and give on-call engineers a safe, idempotent toolkit for production operations.
acceptance_criteria:
1) OCC exposes a CLI and lightweight web UI for 15 most-common ops actions (restarts, scale, KV flush, cache invalidation, snapshot, rollback).
2) At least three critical runbooks (gateway OOM, model-serving hot loop, DB connection storm) are modelled as sequences of tasks with explicit prechecks and rollback steps.
3) Task runner supports dry-run, required-approvals, and automatic audit events sent to audit-log service.
4) Integrations: GitHub PR for task templates, Confluence link for runbook text, Grafana alert->task mapping, and Slack triage channel automation.
5) Post-launch: runbook-task conversions reduce mean manual steps in playbook runs by >=40% in pilot team within 30 days.
implementation_notes:
- Small, incremental PRs: CLI core -> task DSL -> web UI -> automation hooks.
- Prefer idempotent REST actions and read-verify-write patterns for every task.
- Use existing opsctl service as a library where possible to avoid duplicating secrets/credentials management.
- Tasks should be represented as simple YAML templates stored in ops-config Git with CI validation.
- All execution must flow through the centralized task-runner to ensure audit events and TTL-limited service tokens.
- Security review required because several tasks mutate production state and access KMS-backed keys.
steps:
1) Inventory top 20 runbooks and prioritize by incident frequency and customer impact (week 1).
2) Define Task DSL (precheck, execute, verify, revert, metadata) and implement parser (week 2-3).
3) Implement local CLI plugin that can execute tasks in dry-run and live mode, integrating with opsctl auth (week 4).
4) Build minimal web UI for on-call to browse tasks, request approval, and run with a progress console (week 5-7).
5) Hook automation: map Grafana alert rules to suggested task runbooks; implement Slack triage bot to propose tasks on alert (week 8-9).
6) Pilot with Platform SRE team; collect telemetry and iterate (week 10-12).
7) Roll out to Support and Eng teams after pilot validation and security sign-off.
risks:
- Over-automation risk: executing blunt runbook steps without adequate guardrails may increase blast radius. Mitigation: required approvals, dry-run defaults, and auto-revert on failed verification.
- Integration complexity with existing opsctl and IAM systems; mitigation: wrap opsctl as a library and reuse existing tokens and audit pipeline.
- UX confusion across CLI and web: deliver parity and clear guidance, include tour and enforced prechecks.
- Performance: long-running tasks (snapshots) may block operator workflows; design async job model and notify on completion.
